title: SDK morning rituals and chaos safety map
content:
Purpose: a compact, repeatable morning ritual and minimal safety map for engineers running SDK onramps. This is a working sketch intended for developer advocates, onboarding buddies, and engineers shipping SDK-instrumented demos. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-success, catch common regressions quickly, and provide a small decision tree for safe rollbacks and canary kills.

Audience: eng-developer-experience, solutions-engineering, customer-success engineers who run workshops or triage first-run customer issues. Also useful for new hires doing a demo drop-in.

Scope: covers the first 50 minutes of an onramp / sample app setup, quick telemetry checks, minimal smoke commands, a short failure-mode map (chaos safety), and a one-page rollback decision tree. Not a full runbook for infra incidents.

One-line ritual (what to do in the first 10 minutes):
  1) Confirm API key / environment: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY (or use local credentials helper)
  2) Run a deterministic fast smoke call: python examples/hello_sdk.py --sample-token 42 --quick-mode
  3) Check client telemetry in Console > Routes > demo-sample (last 15m) for error spikes and tail latency
  4) If anything fails, capture: logs, last request-id, stdout from sample app, and open ENG-2147 reference template

Why rituals? Most onboarding failures are simple: bad keys, mismatched versions, missing env vars, or local network proxies. A short, repeatable sequence reduces cognitive load and creates consistent triage artifacts to share with support.

Detailed morning checklist (first 50 minutes):
  00-05: Quick creds + environment sanity
    - Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY present and readable by process. If using local sandbox, run: rwctl auth whoami
    - Confirm python/node version matches supported matrix (python 3.10-3.11, node 18+).
  05-15: Minimal smoke - deterministic sample
    - Run the lightweight sample that uses a fixed seed / system prompt: python examples/hello_sdk.py --fast
    - Expected output: JSON with fields: request_id, model, tokens_consumed, stable_text. If output deviates, copy stdout/stderr.
  15-25: Telemetry spot check
    - Open Console > Routes and filter by sample route name. Confirm successful calls in last 15 minutes and tail latency under 300ms for hosted tier.
    - Check token-cost estimate in route details; note if cost spikes unexpectedly.
  25-35: Integrations + network check
    - If using a proxy or enterprise network, validate TLS inspection is off. curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health should return 200.
    - Verify DNS resolves to expected region endpoints if testing private deployments.
  35-45: Quick configuration sanity
    - Confirm SDK version: pip show redwood-sdk or npm ls @redwood/sdk. If mismatched, use the pinned version specified in the playbook.
    - Verify any feature flags required for onramp (e.g., streaming-enabled) via feature flag UI or local override.
  45-50: Final quick smoke and snapshot
    - Re-run the smoke test, capture timings (latency, tokens), and attach to the onboarding ticket.

Minimal smoke commands (copy-paste friendly):
  - rwctl auth whoami
  - python -c "from redwood import Client; print(Client().models.list()[:3])"
  - curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .status

Chaos safety map (top 6 failure modes & quick mitigations):
  A. Missing/rotated API key
    - Symptom: 401/403 on first call.
    - Quick mitigation: confirm env var and rwctl auth. Provide temporary sandbox key if customer blocked.
  B. SDK version mismatch (breaking API change)
    - Symptom: TypeError or missing argument in client constructor.
    - Quick mitigation: pin known-good version in virtualenv, reproduce sample against pinned tag. Raise PR to update onramp template if regression is upstream.
  C. Network corporate proxy/TLS interception
    - Symptom: TLS handshake errors or 526.
    - Quick mitigation: ask customer to whitelist api.redwood.ai, test curl, suggest desktop tethering as isolation test.
  D. Rate-limiting + burst quotas on hosted accounts
    - Symptom: 429 on short bursts during demo.
    - Quick mitigation: throttle demo traffic client-side; request temporary burst increased via ENG-ops or use dedicated dev pool.
  E. Misconfigured private deployment endpoint
    - Symptom: DNS resolves but API returns 404 or incompatible model catalog.
    - Quick mitigation: confirm deployment config, model pin compatibility. Fall back to hosted demo route if allowed.
  F. Regressed streaming API surface
    - Symptom: streaming events truncated or not arriving.
    - Quick mitigation: switch to non-streaming quick path and file regression with sdk-team.

One-page rollback decision tree (short):
  - Is the issue isolated to a single customer/demo? -> yes: revert local feature flag or rotate to hosted sample; no: go to next
  - Is there a failing SDK release in the last 24 hours? -> yes: roll back package pin for demos and open hotfix; no: go to next
  - Are infra health checks failing cluster-wide? -> yes: engage SRE runbook (page id: CON-981), activate incident bridge; no: schedule patch and use canary fallback route

Acceptance checklist before handing an adopter off to customer-success:
  - [ ] Deterministic sample passes locally and in CI (seeded run)
  - [ ] Console telemetry shows consistent success for sample route (last 1h)
  - [ ] Smoke commands documented in the ticket and attached to the demo repo
  - [ ] Any nonstandard networking requirements documented and flagged to solutions engineering

Templates to attach to onboarding ticket (linked_artifacts above):
  - Minimal reproduction README snippet (one-file example)
  - STDOUT capture template (request_id, time, sample input, stdout)
  - Quick triage checklist with expected fields (SDK version, python/node, region)

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
  - Should we add a lightweight rwctl subcommand that runs the full morning ritual and collects a zipped bundle? (Rafael to prototype)
  - Add a minimal node example that exercises streaming fallback to the playbook repo (Linh owns)
  - Decide standard pinned SDK versions for workshops (proposal: latest patch of current minor)

Notes from last workshop (2024-10-28):
  - Most attendees hit proxy/TLS issues; add proxy troubleshooting to the quickstart card.
  - One customer experienced a cost spike due to longer system prompts; added a token estimate note to the sample README.

How to use this doc in practice:
  - Dev advocate / onboarding buddy reads top section aloud when starting a session.
  - Use the smoke commands verbatim in triage tickets to produce consistent artifacts.
  - When in doubt, fall back to the hosted demo route to validate the SDK surface independent of customer infra.

Slack bookmarks / channels: #devexp-onramp, #sdk-triage
Confluence home: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEXP/SDK+Onramp+Home
Jira template: ENG-2147

Small appendix: reproducible hello sample (one-line pseudo-snippet)
  - python examples/hello_sdk.py --system "You are a helpful assistant" --input "hello" --seed 42 --output-format json

End of draft. This is intentionally compact and workshop-oriented — feedback welcome.
